title: Contract-first interface design
subtitle: Every job an agent receives in my governance platform carries a schema that says what must come back. Contracts first, prose only for behaviour.

stats.label: seams in the registry, each with producer, consumer, schema and refusal tests
input contracts and overlays delivered in the first phase
the packet that went out past a ceiling one launch path never checked

lede: In AgentOS, free-form messages between agents were where long runs drifted, so I made every handoff in AgentOS a typed contract from its first phase. That phase delivered the input contracts and overlays under change control, pinned by a hashed manifest. Each task gets an execution contract rendered by AgentOS. Above tasks sit envelopes, the ratified limits of autonomous work. Every seam has a contract pair. The producer validates against a JSON Schema when it builds a payload, and the consumer validates again when it ingests it. Both call one shared validator, so the two sides cannot drift apart, and a refusal names the schema it enforced, which gives an agent something concrete to fix.
quote: A declared limit nobody checks is documentation.
evidence: Contract-first interface design: every agent handoff a typed contract validated by producer and consumer against one JSON Schema, in a registry of 10 seams with refusal tests.
Multi-agent governance: execution contracts that name write roots, sealed dependencies and the evidence a task must return, under envelopes of ratified autonomy.
Limit enforcement at choke points: a packet-size ceiling moved into both choke points after a 4.78 MB packet passed a launch path that never checked it.
author: Corey James
